title: Technical Support & Troubleshooting
description: Diagnose PC, network, and account problems from symptoms and command output using CompTIA's method.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of the CompTIA A+ troubleshooting methodology in order.

lines.text: Establish a theory of probable cause
Test the theory to determine the cause
Establish a plan of action to resolve the problem and implement the solution
Verify full system functionality and, if applicable, implement preventive measures

questions.explanation: CompTIA's six steps run from identifying the problem through theory, testing, planning and implementing, and verifying, ending with documentation. A common mistake is implementing a fix before testing the theory, which leads to changes that don't address the real cause.

questions.prompt: A user says they have "no internet." Their ipconfig output is shown below. What is the most likely cause?

code.source:
Ethernet adapter Ethernet:

   Connection-specific DNS Suffix  . :
   Link-local IPv6 Address . . . . . : fe80::4c1a:9b2e:7d3f:1a2b%12
   Autoconfiguration IPv4 Address. . : 169.254.37.112
   Subnet Mask . . . . . . . . . . . : 255.255.0.0
   Default Gateway . . . . . . . . . :

options.text: The DNS server is down, so the PC can't resolve names to IP addresses
The PC couldn't reach a DHCP server, so Windows assigned itself an APIPA address
A static IP was entered with the wrong subnet mask and no default gateway
Another device on the network is using the same IP address as this PC

questions.explanation: 169.254.x.x with a 255.255.0.0 mask and no gateway is an Automatic Private IP Addressing (APIPA) address, which Windows assigns itself when DHCP gets no answer. Check the cable, switch port or VLAN, and the DHCP service. A DNS outage would leave a valid DHCP address in place.

questions.prompt: A user moved to a new desk and docked their laptop. The laptop screen works, but the external monitor shows "No signal." The same monitor model worked at their old desk yesterday. What should you check first?

options.text: Reinstall the laptop's graphics driver from the manufacturer's site
Swap the monitor for a new one from inventory
Check that the video cable is seated and the monitor's input matches the port in use
Reimage the laptop, since docking problems usually mean OS corruption

questions.explanation: CompTIA's methodology says to question the obvious and check the simple, recent changes first. A move often leaves a loose cable or the monitor set to the wrong input (HDMI vs. DisplayPort). Reinstalling drivers or swapping hardware costs far more time and ignores the change that just happened.

questions.prompt: A workstation can't open \\fileserver01. You run the commands below. What is the most likely cause?

code.source:
C:\> ping 10.0.5.20

Pinging 10.0.5.20 with 32 bytes of data:
Reply from 10.0.5.20: bytes=32 time=2ms TTL=127
Reply from 10.0.5.20: bytes=32 time=1ms TTL=127

C:\> ping fileserver01.corp.example.com
Ping request could not find host fileserver01.corp.example.com. Please check the name and try again.

options.text: The default gateway is misconfigured, so traffic can't leave the local subnet
The file server's firewall is blocking ICMP from this workstation
The NIC driver is corrupt and is dropping outbound packets
Name resolution is failing; check the DNS server settings and the DNS record

questions.explanation: Pinging the server's IP gets replies, so routing, the NIC, and the server's firewall all work. Only resolving the name fails, which points to DNS (the client's DNS server setting or a missing or wrong record). A bad gateway or a blocked ICMP would have made the IP ping fail too.

questions.prompt: After a technician adds a second RAM module, a desktop powers on and its fans spin, but there is no video and it beeps in a repeating pattern. What is the most likely fix?

options.text: Reseat the new module and confirm it matches the board's supported type and speed
Replace the power supply, since it can't handle the extra load from the new RAM
Reinstall the operating system, since the new RAM corrupted the boot files
Update the graphics driver, since the beeps are a video driver error code

questions.explanation: Repeating beeps with no video right after a memory change point to a POST memory failure: a module that isn't fully seated or is incompatible. The OS and drivers haven't loaded at this stage of POST, so they can't be the cause.

questions.prompt: One laptop can't reach intranet.corp.example.com, while coworkers on the same network can. You collect the output below. What is the cause?

code.source:
C:\> ipconfig /all
   ...
   DHCP Enabled. . . . . . . . . . . : Yes
   IPv4 Address. . . . . . . . . . . : 10.20.4.88(Preferred)
   DNS Servers . . . . . . . . . . . : 8.8.8.8
                                       1.1.1.1

C:\> nslookup intranet.corp.example.com
Server:  dns.google
Address:  8.8.8.8

*** dns.google can't find intranet.corp.example.com: Non-existent domain

options.text: The intranet web server is down, so its DNS record was removed
The laptop has no route to the corporate network, so the lookup times out
The laptop is set to public DNS servers, which can't resolve internal names
The laptop's hosts file is redirecting intranet to the wrong IP address

questions.explanation: The adapter is using 8.8.8.8 and 1.1.1.1, and Google's resolver correctly answers "Non-existent domain" because the zone exists only on internal DNS. Set the adapter back to the DHCP-provided DNS servers. If the hosts file were the cause, nslookup (which queries DNS directly) would still have succeeded.

questions.prompt: A user changed her password Monday morning. Since then her account locks out roughly every 30 minutes; it never happened before. The domain controller's lockout event is shown below (MAIL-GW01 handles mobile mail sync). What is the most likely cause?

code.source:
Event ID: 4740  A user account was locked out.
Account That Was Locked Out:
   Account Name:          m.rivera
Additional Information:
   Caller Computer Name:  MAIL-GW01

options.text: A device still has her old password, such as her phone's mail app syncing via MAIL-GW01
MAIL-GW01's computer account is corrupt, and the server must be rejoined to the domain
Her new password breaks complexity rules, so the domain controller keeps rejecting it
AD replication is incomplete, so MAIL-GW01 is locking accounts on its own schedule

questions.explanation: Lockouts that start right after a password change and come from a sync service are the classic sign of a device retrying cached old credentials. Updating or removing the account on her phone (and any saved credentials) stops them. A password that broke the complexity rules would have been rejected when she tried to set it.

questions.prompt: Every user of a shared Windows print server sees jobs stuck at "Error - Printing" on three different printers. Each printer prints a test page from its own front panel without trouble. What should you do next?

options.text: Replace the toner and fuser on each printer, since all three show an error status
Clear the stuck jobs and restart the Print Spooler service on the print server
Reinstall the printer drivers on every client workstation that uses these printers
Factory-reset each printer and re-enter its network settings from scratch

questions.explanation: The printers work on their own, and the fault spans several printers that share one server, so the common component, the server's spooler, is the likely cause. Clients and printer hardware are the wrong layer to fix when every queue on that server is stuck.

questions.prompt: A caller says she is the CFO, is traveling, and urgently needs her password reset. She gives her employee ID and her manager's name. Select the TWO actions that follow good support practice.

options.text: Verify identity with the documented method, such as a callback to the number on file
Reset the password, since she knows her employee ID and her manager's name
If she can't be verified, decline the reset and escalate per policy, however urgent it seems
Email a temporary password to the personal address she gives you on the call
Temporarily turn off MFA on her account so she can sign in from the hotel

questions.explanation: Urgency and authority are classic social-engineering pressures, and employee IDs and org charts are easy for an attacker to find. Follow the identity-verification procedure and escalate if it fails. Sending credentials to an unverified address or removing MFA hands the account to whoever is calling.

questions.prompt: A laptop's clock resets to January 2019 every time it fully loses power. Afterward, domain sign-in on the office network fails with "There is a time and/or date difference between the client and server," while sign-in with cached credentials works off-network. What fixes this?

options.text: Remove the laptop from the domain and rejoin it to repair the computer account trust
Reset the user's password in Active Directory and have them sign in with the new one
Flush the DNS cache and re-register the laptop's DNS record with the domain controller
Replace the CMOS/RTC battery and resync the clock, since Kerberos allows about 5 minutes of skew

questions.explanation: Kerberos rejects authentication when the client and domain controller clocks differ by more than the default 5 minutes, and a clock that resets on power loss points to a dead CMOS/RTC battery. Rejoining the domain fixes broken trust relationships, not time skew, and the error message names time specifically.

questions.prompt: You rolled back a faulty network driver, and the user's laptop now gets a valid IP address. Per the CompTIA methodology, what should happen before you document and close the ticket?

options.text: Have the user confirm normal work (VPN, email, file shares) and block the bad driver from redeploying
Close the ticket right away, because a valid IP address proves the network problem is fully resolved
Escalate the ticket to tier 2 so a senior technician can review the rollback before closure
Reimage the laptop anyway to be certain no other driver problems remain on the system

questions.explanation: Step 5 is to verify full system functionality and, if applicable, implement preventive measures, such as stopping the update tool from pushing the faulty driver again. An IP address alone doesn't prove the user can work, and reimaging is unnecessary disruption.

questions.prompt: A user reports that an application hosted at 203.0.113.80 is slow. A junior technician sends this traceroute and says hops 3 and 4 are "down." What is the correct reading?

code.source:
C:\> tracert -d 203.0.113.80

Tracing route to 203.0.113.80 over a maximum of 30 hops

  1    <1 ms    <1 ms    <1 ms  10.0.0.1
  2     9 ms     8 ms     9 ms  198.51.100.1
  3     *        *        *     Request timed out.
  4     *        *        *     Request timed out.
  5    24 ms    23 ms    25 ms  203.0.113.80

Trace complete.

options.text: Hops 3 and 4 are dropping all traffic, so open a ticket with the ISP to get those routers fixed
Hops 3 and 4 probably just don't answer traceroute probes; the destination replies in ~24 ms
The trace is incomplete, so rerun it with a larger packet size to force replies from hops 3 and 4
Hops 3 and 4 are firewalls blocking the application's port, which explains why it is slow

questions.explanation: If those routers were dropping traffic, hop 5 could never reply. Routers often rate-limit or don't send ICMP Time Exceeded, so asterisks at intermediate hops are normal when the destination answers. The 24 ms path is healthy, so look at the server or application next.

questions.prompt: Users intermittently lose connection to an app server at 10.0.20.15, whose NIC MAC address is 3c-52-82-1a-9e-04. A technician checks a client's ARP cache twice, 15 minutes apart. What is the most likely cause, and what is the next step?

code.source:
09:02  C:\> arp -a 10.0.20.15
  Internet Address      Physical Address      Type
  10.0.20.15            3c-52-82-1a-9e-04     dynamic

09:17  C:\> arp -a 10.0.20.15
  Internet Address      Physical Address      Type
  10.0.20.15            00-1b-a9-6c-22-f1     dynamic

options.text: The server's NIC is failing intermittently; replace the NIC and monitor the server
The client's ARP cache timeout is too short; increase it with a registry change
Another device is answering ARP for 10.0.20.15; trace 00-1b-a9-6c-22-f1 in the switch MAC table
DNS has two A records for the server; delete the stale record and flush client caches

questions.explanation: The same IP resolving to two different MACs means a second device is claiming the address, usually a static IP inside the DHCP scope (or ARP spoofing). Finding the switch port that learned the second MAC locates the device. DNS maps names to IPs and plays no part in the IP-to-MAC mapping.

questions.prompt: Over the site-to-site VPN, users can ping a file server and open small web pages, but large file copies and some HTTPS pages hang. The tests below are run from a client. What is the most likely cause and fix?

code.source:
C:\> ping -f -l 1472 10.50.0.10
Pinging 10.50.0.10 with 1472 bytes of data:
Packet needs to be fragmented but DF set.
Packet needs to be fragmented but DF set.

C:\> ping -f -l 1372 10.50.0.10
Pinging 10.50.0.10 with 1372 bytes of data:
Reply from 10.50.0.10: bytes=1372 time=31ms TTL=126

options.text: The VPN is bandwidth-throttled; ask the ISP to raise the circuit's speed
Large packets are dropped by a congested link; enable QoS for file traffic
The client MTU is too small; raise it to 9000 to enable jumbo frames
VPN overhead lowers the path MTU; clamp TCP MSS or lower the tunnel MTU

questions.explanation: A 1472-byte DF ping (1500 bytes on the wire) can't pass, but a 1372-byte one can, so encapsulation has cut the usable MTU below 1500. Small exchanges work while full-size segments stall, because ICMP "fragmentation needed" messages are filtered somewhere on the return path, so Path MTU Discovery fails for those flows. MSS clamping on the VPN gateway is the standard fix, and jumbo frames make it worse.

questions.prompt: A user's laptop freezes when opening files. SMART shows the reallocated sector count climbing and 40 pending sectors. The user asks you to run chkdsk /r overnight to "fix the bad sectors." What should you do first?

options.text: Run chkdsk /r first so the bad sectors are repaired before the backup copies anything
Back up or image the user's data now, using a tool that tolerates read errors, then replace the drive
Defragment the drive so the data moves away from the failing area of the disk
Reinstall Windows over the existing installation to replace any corrupted system files

questions.explanation: Rising reallocated and pending sectors mean the drive is failing, and chkdsk /r reads every sector, which stresses the disk and can make it fail before the data is recovered. Following CompTIA's "perform backups before making changes," secure the data first, then replace the hardware.
